title: RunRecord
description: An append-oriented, machine-readable record of one orchestration run, stored as provenance/runs/<run_id>.json. Captures the route_task decision verbatim (never reinterpreted), the delegated steps actually executed, and their worker/model attribution and outcomes, where observable. Distinct from backlog items (durable task metadata in backlog/backlog.yaml) and GitHub Issues (human-facing collaboration surface). A field whose value the orchestrator cannot observe MUST be explicit null (or the literal string "unknown" for free-text fields where a string is required) -- never a guessed value.

worker_overrides.description: Each time a terminal worker record was replaced: by the lead (completed -> failed/blocked, failed -> blocked, or a failed/blocked worker restated with a different blocker code), or failed -> completed when a later start of the same step succeeded (by lead or extension, reason retry_succeeded). The earlier status and blocker code are kept here; the worker holds the current ones.

phase_status.description: Status of the worker's phase when the override was recorded; a terminal value flags a phase outcome recorded before the override.

reason.description: retry_succeeded: a retry of a failed step succeeded and replaced the failure (lead or extension). prerequisite_blocker: a failure with a prerequisite code (or blocker_kind prerequisite) made the step blocked with that code. repeated_ineffective_action: the extension refused another start of a step whose failure signature used up its retry budget and blocked it. retry_gate: the step was already blocked for another reason (a prerequisite) and the extension refused a later start as a repeated ineffective action. state_changed: a step blocked that way was reopened as failed because its checkout HEAD or declared inputs changed.

worker_sandbox.description: The OS sandbox posture the lifecycle extension applied to this run's Claude workers (#63), one entry per run start or resume (consecutive identical entries are kept once; the first, pinning entry is never trimmed). state enabled is the default; opted_out is only the user's explicit PI_ORCHESTRATOR_WORKER_SANDBOX=0 (source env). allowed_domains and cache_directories are the widening workers actually used: from .pi/autonomy.yaml on the repository's default branch on GitHub (policy_source default_branch, at policy_commit), empty when the default branch has no policy (default), when it could not be read (unavailable) or is invalid (invalid). The first entry pins the run's widening; a later entry never widens it, and what it asked beyond the pin is in refused_allowed_domains / refused_cache_directories. local_drift: the checkout's own copy declares a different worker_sandbox (informational, never used). user_settings_widening: widening keys present in the user's own Claude Code settings, which merge into every worker's settings (recorded only). Sandbox denials inside a worker are not recorded here: Claude Code reports them to the model, not in its JSON result.

failure_retry_budget.description: The per-signature retry budget the lifecycle extension applied to this run, and where it came from. Absent until the first retry gate.

failure_signatures.description: Structured failure signatures of worker steps, oldest first (bounded: the oldest non-blocked entry is dropped when full). A signature is (task, step, route epoch, route, failure code, checkout HEAD, declared-input digest); `digest` is the SHA-256 of those fields. `count` is how many times that exact signature failed. Entries with kind `prerequisite` record an unresolved prerequisite (a blocked step with its own code) and never count toward a loop. When a counted signature has more failures than the retry budget allows, the next start of the step is refused and the entry is marked `blocked` (step blocked with REPEATED_INEFFECTIVE_ACTION). A successful retry of the step clears its entries.

head.description: Checkout HEAD at the failure (a new HEAD is a different signature).

reconciled.description: Phases and workers that were still open when the run ended without COMPLETED. Each is set to abandoned; from_status keeps what was recorded. Absent on records that ended with nothing open.

wave_id.description: Id of a reconciled wave (kind wave): declared or integrating when the run ended without COMPLETED.

route_epoch.description: Route epoch of a reconciled worker.

routing.description: Compact policy decision metadata for the viewer. No task prose or repository evidence. Absent on historical runs.

path_floor_matches.description: Path floors matched by the task's declared files_or_areas before the run. Absent when none matched.

escalations.description: Append-only authorized route changes. The phase route and routing fields retain the initial decision. PATH_FLOOR entries are written only by an underrated post-diff check (diff_floor_checks); their to_route may equal from_route (a capacity-only raise).

paths.description: PATH_FLOOR only: the floored changed paths. The route result that confirms the re-route must pass the post-diff check against them.

required_capacities.description: PATH_FLOOR only: the capacity tier per step the engine required.

diff_floor_checks.description: Post-diff path-floor checks of the task's bound worktrees at integrate_begin, latest last. An underrated check (CLASSIFICATION_UNDERRATED_BY_DIFF) also appended a PATH_FLOOR escalation to to_route.

wave_id.description: The wave this routed task (phase) last ran in. Absent for tasks never declared in a wave.

workspace_bound.description: A worktree was bound for a step of this task and no integrated wave has covered the task since: a mutating worker may have run, so it must be integrated before COMPLETED.

bound_epochs.description: Route epochs in which a worktree was bound for this task; an escalation does not forget the old route's.

route_epoch.description: Zero for initial routing; increments for each authorized phase escalation. Missing on historical workers means zero.

auto_recorded.description: The lifecycle extension recorded this worker (start or terminal status). A lead restatement of it is then accepted leniently: the same model spelled canonically or not, a different reasoning effort (the routed plan's value stays), and an in_progress after a terminal status are no-ops.

owner_id.description: Recorded owner of the run (audit A3): set at start, by a verified resume and by a takeover. Writes require the run lease, or a free lease and this owner. Absent or null on unowned and historical runs, which accept any writer while no lease exists.

checkpoint.description: Resume checkpoint (audit A10): the parent checkout's resolved path, branch (null when detached) and HEAD (null without commits) at the latest phase boundary, worker approval, integration start, integrated wave or recorded mutation. A resumed run is compared with it before any mutation. Absent on historical records, whose resume is therefore refused.

resume_checks.description: Append-only results of comparing the checkpoint with the live checkout when another process resumed the run. Drift or a missing checkpoint refuses the resume and leaves the run IN_PROGRESS for an operator; nothing is re-based.

previous_owner_id.description: Recorded owner when the check ran. A verified check by another owner changed ownership from this value to owner_id.

lease_takeovers.description: Explicit recoveries of a stale run lease (audit A3), recorded before the lease is replaced. A live lease is never taken over.

forced.description: True when the expired holder was still running on this machine and an explicit force reason displaced it.

waves.description: Waves of routed tasks with disjoint write scopes that ran concurrently, in declaration order, with their integration state. Absent on historical records.

activity.description: Recent metadata-only worker interactions for live viewers. No prompts or outputs.

route.description: Routed route of the task, recorded by the lifecycle extension at worker start.

prompt_excerpt.description: First 300 characters of the worker contract after its task tag and goal line, control characters removed, secret-like spans masked before the cut. The full text lives in the Pi session transcript.

goal.description: The contract's one-sentence goal line (Goal: ...), bounded and masked like the excerpt.

result_summary.description: First 600 characters of the worker's final text, control characters removed, secret-like text withheld. The full text lives in the Pi session transcript.

result_digest.description: SHA-256 of the worker's full final text.

commit_sha.description: Commit the worker's result reported, when it named one.

interactions.description: Numbered, concise parent-authored summaries of directives, worker feedback, and parent decisions. No prompts, transcripts, hidden reasoning, or raw outputs. Absent on older runs.

context.description: Parent-session context telemetry: observed baseline/peak tokens, Pi compactions, explicit checkpoint references, and accumulated per-backend worker usage. Unobserved counters are null. Absent on historical records.

peak_concurrent_workers.description: Most worker calls observed in flight at once by the lifecycle extension.

worker_active_ms.description: Observed wall-clock time with at least one worker call in flight.

estimated_cost_usd.description: Pi-reported list-price estimate of the lead's own calls; absent when unreported.

cost_complete.description: False once any lead call had tokens but no (or a zero) cost.

lead_call_limit.description: Present only when the run had a lead-call limit: the effective limit, where it came from, the warning threshold and the call it fired at, the lead call count when the limit was reached, and whether the lifecycle extension stopped the run at the limit. A stop leaves the run IN_PROGRESS (stopped_reason LEAD_CALL_LIMIT) with a fresh resume checkpoint; it is resumable only with a raised limit.

calls_seen.description: The lifecycle extension's own lead call count from its limit events; the run's count is the larger of this and the recorded lead_calls.

mid_integration.description: The stop came while a wave was integrating: the pre-integration checkpoint was kept, so a resume reports drift and needs reconciliation.

refused_sets.description: Later limit settings that differed from the limit the launcher pinned and were refused (a forged raise).

lead_calls.description: Observed assistant model calls, in order; task_type is null when attribution is ambiguous or routing has not completed.

authorization.description: How a GitHub write (publication, or an issue/comment batch) was authorized: the autonomy policy on the default branch on GitHub. one_shot_grant, granted_by and granted appear only in records written before the Garden one-shot grant was removed (#59).

permissions.description: The policy permissions this write required; all were granted.

policy_commit.description: The default-branch commit whose .pi/autonomy.yaml authorized the write.

route_task_result.description: The tools/route_task.py result object, stored verbatim (byte-for-byte equal to what route_task returned). This module never reinterprets or revalidates routing semantics -- schemas/execution-plan.schema.json and tools/routing_engine.py remain the sole authority for that.

routing_telemetry.description: Structured observational telemetry for the routing adapter call (timing, byte counts, token/cost counters if exposed). Never influences route_task output or routing policy decisions; null when unobserved.

orchestration_metrics.description: Observational run-level delegation metrics. Missing/unobservable values are explicit null. These metrics never change routing/delegation inside the active run; they support offline benchmark analysis and reviewed policy updates.

trace_schema_version.description: Version of the deterministic trace-rendering contract (tools/provenance.py build_trace_report/render_trace_text and tools/backlog.py trace). Intentionally NOT in `required`: records written before this field existed remain valid and are rendered tolerantly. New records written by this module always set it to 1.

path_floor_match.description: One .pi/routing.yaml path_floors rule matched by a task's declared files_or_areas or by its real diff (tools/routing_engine.py match_path_floors).

rule.description: Index of the rule in its source's list.

step.description: One delegated execution-plan step actually performed during the run. Field names mirror schemas/execution-plan.schema.json where applicable (role/family/capacity/context/fresh-context/mutation), plus resolved context-window and attribution/outcome fields that execution plans intentionally do not carry.

execution_plan_step_id.description: The matching step id from the run's route_task_result.execution_plan.steps, if this step corresponds to one.

backend.description: Concrete backend/tool actually invoked (e.g. 'spawn_subagent', 'AskClaude'), if observable.

model.description: Concrete model identifier actually used, if observable. Never guessed -- null when not exposed by the backend.

capacity_tier.description: Capacity tier actually requested for this step, if observable.

context_strategy.description: Context strategy actually requested for this step, if observable.

context_window_tier.description: Resolved context-window tier actually used, if observable.

worker_identifier.description: Worker/subagent/session identifier, if available from the backend.

outcome.description: Free-text summary of the step's outcome (e.g. 'accepted', 'repaired once', 'rejected'). Use 'unknown' rather than guessing when unobservable.

anyOf.description: Legacy/simple form: a command string with no observed result. Rendered as result 'unknown'.

returned_artifacts.description: Compact summaries of artifacts a step actually returned (a spec, a diff summary, a review, a validation report). Never stores artifact bodies, diffs, stdout, transcripts, or prompt content -- `summary` is a short description and `reference` is a repository-relative path or stable external reference. Not in `required`: absent on historical records and simply rendered as '(none observed)'.

category.description: Mirrors routing/default-policy.yaml's review_findings categories (that file remains the sole source of truth for the category list).

repair_of.description: task_id of the step this step repairs, if this step is a repair.

reasoning_setting.description: Reasoning/thinking effort setting actually used, if observable. Not free-form hidden reasoning.

telemetry.description: Structured observational telemetry for this delegated step (timing, byte counts, token/cost counters if exposed). Never contains prompts, transcripts, hidden reasoning, or secrets; null when unobserved.

cache_write_tokens.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache, billed as input unlike cache reads; absent in records that predate it.

cost_complete.description: False once any usage event had no cost, or a zero cost despite tokens.

observational_telemetry.description: Closed, structured observational telemetry. All unobserved values are explicit null. This object is for counters/timing only and must not contain prompts, transcripts, hidden reasoning, credentials, or secret-like fields.

cached_tokens.description: Cached/read-from-cache token count if explicitly exposed by the backend; null when unavailable.

orchestration_metrics.description: Run-level metrics for evaluating whether delegation improved speed/cost/quality. Derived fields are computed only when their required explicit baselines are available.
